calls.summary: Priya Sundaram called to set up a consultation for a bulk Visa prepaid gift card order for her firm's client appreciation program. Agent Oscar walked her through denominations and the $5.95 activation fee, then booked a program consultation for the following week. She confirmed the details happily before ending the call.

Marcus DeLeon called to check the order status on a batch of eGift card links he purchased through Giftcards.com. Agent Lila confirmed the links had been delivered to his recipient list and resent one that had bounced. Marcus thanked her and no further action was needed.

Angela Rhodes reached out about launching a corporate rewards and incentives program for her sales team. Agent Rosey explained the customizable reward tiers and volume pricing, then scheduled a consultation with an enterprise specialist. Angela was enthusiastic and provided her team headcount.

Daniel Ortega called as a new customer to schedule a consultation about a Visa gift card disbursement program for employee rebates. Agent Lee collected his full contact details, company name, and estimated order volume, then booked the intake consultation. Daniel confirmed the appointment time and appreciated the clear next steps.

Sophia Chen wanted to discuss sending eGift cards on social channels for a holiday promotion. Agent Mary described the digital gifting options and shareable link delivery, then scheduled a consultation to scope the campaign. Sophia agreed and shared her preferred callback window.

Robert Ellison inquired about a prepaid card disbursement solution for corporate refund payouts. Agent Sue outlined the digital and physical prepaid options and booked a consultation with the payments team. Robert had a few pricing questions that were noted for the specialist.

Nadia Foster called about a delayed same-day delivery on a multi-brand gift card order. Agent Mike located the order and found a fulfillment hold, then escalated it for expedited shipping. Nadia was frustrated but calmer after he confirmed a revised delivery date.

Helen Marsh called to explore a gift card program management contract for her retail chain. Agent Rose explained issuance and fulfillment services and scheduled a consultation with the enterprise team. Helen was interested but hesitant about onboarding timelines.

Gregory Paulson disputed a duplicate charge on a prepaid Mastercard gift card he purchased. Agent Oscar reviewed the transaction history and opened a billing investigation. Gregory remained annoyed that a resolution would take a few business days.

Tanya Brooks called because her Tap to Pay Visa gift card would not activate in the MyCardWallet app. Agent Lila attempted a card activation reset and filed a replacement request when it failed. Tanya was upset about the delay before her trip.

Victor Nunez called to cancel a corporate rewards order that had already been submitted. Agent Lee explained the cancellation window and processing steps, then logged the request. Victor was displeased that part of the order had already been fulfilled.

Denise Kwan complained that a batch of single-brand retailer gift cards arrived with incorrect balances after activation. Agent Mary apologized and started a reconciliation case with the fulfillment team. Denise stayed frustrated about the impact on her event.

Franklin Reyes left a voicemail asking about the status of a delayed prepaid Visa gift card refund. No agent was available and the call rolled to voicemail. His message was logged for a callback the next business day.

Marion Whitfield called angry that a Visa gift card she received as a corporate reward was declined at checkout despite showing a balance. Agent Mike checked the account and found a merchant filter block, then escalated the case. Marion demanded a supervisor before the call ended.

transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling Blackhawk Network. This is Marcus Bell speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, yes, thanks for picking up. My name is Jennifer Hobbs. We run a regional retail chain with about 28 locations, and we're looking to launch a corporate gift card program for our customers and employees. I found BHN on a search and thought you might be a good fit.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Jennifer, that's fantastic. We work with retailers just like you. Can you tell me a little bit more about what you're hoping to achieve with a gift card program? Are you looking at customer rewards, employee recognition, or maybe both?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Both, actually. Our customers keep asking for gift cards to give to friends and family, and we also want to use them internally to recognize top performing staff. So we need something flexible and integrated with our point of sale.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. That's a really common use case, and our platform handles both consumer gifting and employee rewards on a single integration. Just to make sure I'm serving you well, what region are you operating in? What's your primary ZIP code?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We're based in Southern California, 90210 is our main office.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, we definitely serve that area. And just to confirm, your business name is?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hobbs Retail Group, H-O-B-B-S.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, I've got that. And the best phone number to reach you is still ****?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent, Jennifer. So here's what I'd like to do. I'd like to schedule a formal consultation with our solutions team. They'll dive deeper into your specific use case, walk through our issuance platform, pricing, and how we'd integrate with your point of sale. How does your schedule look over the next two weeks?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Um, we're pretty busy right now, but I think I could do next Thursday afternoon if that works. Maybe around 2 PM?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Next Thursday at 2 PM works great. I'm going to get you on the calendar with our enterprise team. They'll send you a meeting confirmation with the details.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay, sounds good. Should I prepare anything for the call, or just come with questions?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Just come ready to talk through your current setup and what success looks like for your organization. Our team will take it from there. You're all set, Jennifer. Thanks for choosing Blackhawk Network, and we'll see you next Thursday at 2 PM.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you, Marcus.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Jennifer. Have a great day.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Hobbs from Hobbs Retail Group, a 28-location Southern California retailer, called to explore Blackhawk Network's gift card solutions for both customer gifting and employee rewards. Marcus successfully qualified the prospect, confirmed her service area and contact details, and scheduled a consultation with the enterprise team for the following Thursday at 2 PM. While the call was well-structured and the booking was secured, Marcus missed capturing Jennifer's email address and did not set specific expectations about what materials she should review prior to the consultation or how the integration process would unfold.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, great work on this intake call. You opened strong with a clear greeting, asked open-ended qualifying questions, and listened well to Jennifer's dual use case. Your pace was conversational and you confirmed back key details like the spelling of her business name and ZIP code. Two quick coaching notes. First, make sure to capture the prospect's email before the close so you can send pre-consultation prep materials and a calendar invite with more context about what the consultation will cover. Second, take 30 seconds to set expectations for the call itself. Tell them what to have handy, mention that you'll discuss timeline and pricing, and let them know what BHN will need from them to prepare a demo. Both moves will increase their engagement and show preparation.

brandConversationRules: Intro and offer: Introduce yourself as Blackhawk Network's AI agent here to help build a personalized branded payments quote, mention that new enterprise programs can lock in preferred volume pricing this quarter, and ask if they would like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask the key questions one at a time, how many cards or rewards they need, the denomination or load amount per card, the product type (Visa or Mastercard prepaid, eGift links, single-brand or multi-brand, or a full incentives program), their target launch timeline, and finally the company ZIP code so we can confirm distribution and delivery availability.

Estimate then book: Confirm we support their ZIP for distribution, share a preliminary per-card price range based on the volume and product they described, recommend a consultation with a BHN branded payments specialist for an exact quote, propose a specific day and time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer Visa and Mastercard prepaid gift cards?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer open-loop Visa and Mastercard prepaid gift cards in customizable denominations for gifting and disbursement. I can set up a consultation to match the right card program to your needs.

qaPairs.question: Can I send digital gift cards instantly?
qaPairs.answer: Absolutely, our eGift card links deliver instantly as shareable links for text, email, or social channels. Let's book a quick consultation to configure your digital gifting program.

qaPairs.question: What is the difference between single-brand and multi-brand cards?
qaPairs.answer: Single-brand cards are redeemable at one retailer, while multi-brand cards work across a themed bundle of partner brands. A specialist can walk you through which fits your recipients on a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you handle corporate rewards and incentives?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our incentives programs deliver customizable rewards that motivate consumers, employees, and sales teams to take specific actions. I would recommend a consultation to scope your reward volumes and pricing.

qaPairs.question: Can you manage employee recognition rewards?
qaPairs.answer: We offer reloadable reward cards and points-based redemption built for workforce engagement. Let's schedule a consultation to design a program around your team size.

qaPairs.question: How do corporate payouts and disbursements work?
qaPairs.answer: We deliver digital and prepaid disbursements for rebates, refunds, and benefits through a single integration. A specialist can review your disbursement flow during a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer an API for eGift issuance?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our platform supports integrated eGift issuance so you can automate delivery at scale. Book a consultation and our specialist can review the technical fit.

qaPairs.question: What is Tap to Pay on your prepaid cards?
qaPairs.answer: Our Tap to Pay Visa gift cards ship in tamper-evident packaging with no printed account data, and funds are accessed by tapping at contactless terminals or through the MyCardWallet app. I can arrange a consultation to explain the security features.

qaPairs.question: How much do your prepaid cards cost?
qaPairs.answer: Card fees vary by product, denomination, and volume, so I would not want to quote an exact number here. Let's set up a consultation where a specialist can give you an accurate quote.

qaPairs.question: Can you fulfill large gift card orders?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we manage issuance, card production, processing, fulfillment, and settlement across a global network. A consultation is the best way to plan your volume and timeline.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer same-day delivery?
qaPairs.answer: Digital gift cards and eGift links can deliver same day, while physical cards ship on a fulfillment schedule. Let's book a consultation to confirm timing for your program.

qaPairs.question: What is Giftcards.com?
qaPairs.answer: Giftcards.com is our direct-to-consumer storefront offering digital and physical gift cards from hundreds of brand partners. For business programs, I would recommend a consultation with a specialist.

qaPairs.question: Can I brand the cards with my company logo?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we support branded card production and customized digital gifting experiences. A specialist can review branding options during your consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer fraud protection?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our branded payment services include advanced fraud protection across issuance and distribution. Let's schedule a consultation to review the safeguards for your program.

qaPairs.question: How quickly can we launch a program?
qaPairs.answer: Launch timelines depend on program complexity and volume, and many programs move quickly with our single integration. Book a consultation and a specialist can map out your timeline.

qaPairs.question: Do you serve international recipients?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our network spans the globe with more than 400,000 consumer touchpoints. A consultation will let us confirm coverage for the regions you need.

qaPairs.question: What denominations are available?
qaPairs.answer: Denominations range widely, for example eGifts from ten to five hundred dollars, and can be tailored to your program. Let's book a consultation to set your denomination structure.

qaPairs.question: Can rewards be redeemed as points?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our recognition and rewards bundles support points-based redemption alongside reloadable cards. A specialist can design the redemption experience on a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer volume or bulk pricing?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer volume-based pricing for bulk rewards and enterprise programs. I would recommend a consultation so a specialist can prepare accurate figures for your quantities.

qaPairs.question: How do I get a quote for my company?
qaPairs.answer: The best next step is a consultation with a BHN branded payments specialist who can build a quote around your volume, products, and timeline. I can find a day and time that works for you right now.
